Thanks Tom (and Anna). 9/21 2:00–3:00pm PT works for our team — I booked the slot and sent a calendar invite. Preliminary runbook & pre-reqs:

Pre-reqs we will send before the call (by EOD 9/17):
- Staging account details + sample token-based credentials (instructions in attached txt)
- Preferred model specs you want tested (quantized vs fp16) — please attach if you have a preference
- Traffic stub (JMeter or CSV driver) — Tom said he'll share; that will help Marissa tune the harness.

Bench plan highlights:
- Duration: 10 minute bursts, repeated 3x with 5 minute cool-downs between runs; 30m total for active benching during session if we demo live.
- Targets: baseline steady token throughput target 500k tokens/min; burst target 1.5M tokens/min (10m window); 99th-pct latency target <= 450ms at seq_len=512 with KV warm-start.
- Cold-start scenario: synthetic prefix load recommended (we will provide a small warm-up script to approximate production prefixes). Expect ~30–60s ramp for initial KV population depending on model size.
- Metrics collection: per-token latency histogram, p95/p99/p99.9, CPU/GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sampling), network I/O. We'll push a Grafana link and an ingestion endpoint.
- Fallbacks: we'll propose a quantized 8-bit variant and a regional routing fallback for sustained heavy load.

Action items assigned:
- Tom: share traffic stubs and confirm model variants to test (due 9/17).
- Anna: confirm attendee list and any security checklist items for staging access (due 9/17).
- Marissa: prepare the harness and run a dry-run on Redwood staging (Marissa will schedule internally).
- Karthik: prepare a short deck explaining kernel selection & expected latency knobs (3 slides).

Attachments: acme-proposed-agenda.pdf, redwood-staging-access-instructions.txt

Looking forward — see you on Tue 9/21.
